title: On the Benchmarking of LLMs for Open-Domain Dialogue Evaluation

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying existing open-domain dialogue evaluation benchmarks to identify their exclusive focus on the English language and translated English data, which limits their cross-lingual applicability and introduces an English-centric bias into quality assessments.

Analyzing current evaluation metrics and benchmark criteria to show they fail to capture non-Western cultural communication nuances, such as high-context communication, expressions of politeness, idiomatic expressions, and cultural references.

Discussing and analyzing the tendency of LLM-based evaluators to erroneously overlook their own errors or favor their own generated text, particularly during subjective assessments like 'Overall Quality'.

Evaluating the limitations of human annotation by reflecting on how using a small pool of expert annotators with shared Western cultural and professional backgrounds introduces subjective bias into dialogue quality assessments.
